patterns.name: Ledger lines (minimal)
patterns.summary: One aligned, permanent line per step printed as the step finishes, led by a word badge (ok / warn / FAIL), with one transient console.status spinner for the step in flight. No Live, no Progress, no title; TTY and non-TTY output are the same lines.

SUCCESS (TTY, final frame)

  ok    identify Git top-level       C:\src\acme
  ok    configure pre-commit hooks   prek.toml updated, 2 hooks added
  ok    prek install                 Git shims already installed
  ok    prek update --check          hook revisions up to date
  ok    detect-secrets scan          .secrets.baseline created
pkgdx init: done in 2.9s

(while running, a single transient line sits under the ledger:)
⠹ prek update --check ...

WARN (TTY, final frame)
  ok    identify project root        C:\src\acme (pyproject.toml)
  warn  identify Git top-level       not a Git repository, using project root
        -> Run `git init` to enable pre-commit hooks
  ok    configure pre-commit hooks   prek.toml unchanged
  ok    prek install                 Git shims installed at project root
  warn  prek update --check          pkgdx v0.4.2 -> v0.5.0 available
        -> Update remote hook revisions - `prek update`
  ok    detect-secrets scan          .secrets.baseline exists, reused
pkgdx init: done in 2.9s with 2 warnings

FAIL (TTY, final frame)
  ok    identify project root        C:\src\acme (pyproject.toml)
  ok    identify Git top-level       C:\src\acme
  FAIL  configure pre-commit hooks   prek.toml could not be parsed
        Invalid value (at line 12, column 9)
        -> Fix prek.toml, or regenerate it with `pkgdx init --reset`
pkgdx init: failed at step 3/6 (3 steps not run)
patterns.step_states: pending: not shown | running: transient console.status line, 'dots' spinner + label + '...' | ok: 'ok' green | warn: 'warn' bold yellow + indented '->' hint line | fail: 'FAIL' bold red reverse-free, uppercase so it differs from ok/warn without colour, + message line + '->' hint
patterns.header: None. The command name appears once, in the closing summary line.
patterns.success_summary: 'pkgdx init: done in <elapsed>' (plus ' with N warnings' when relevant), one line.
patterns.warning_presentation: Inline under the step that warned: the warn badge, the detail in the detail column, and an indented '->' next-action line. Nothing is logged above the ledger; the warning logging moves out of _core into the CLI layer.
patterns.failure_presentation: Inline at the failing step: FAIL badge, cause in the detail column, raw parser message indented beneath, '->' next action, then the summary line naming the step number and how many steps did not run. No traceback for expected errors; with -d the logger's traceback prints after the ledger. Ctrl-C: the status line is replaced by '  stop  prek update --check   interrupted' and 'pkgdx init: interrupted, no cleanup performed', exit 130.
patterns.state_change_reporting: The detail column of every step always shows Result.detail (created / updated / unchanged / reused), so state changes are visible by default without -d.
patterns.non_tty_behaviour: Identical lines without ANSI and without the status spinner (Rich drops styling on a non-terminal console). Each line is printed when its step finishes, so a CI log streams. Example: '  ok    prek update --check          hook revisions up to date' ... 'pkgdx init: done in 2.9s'.
rich_primitives: Table.grid (one-row grid per step with fixed column widths)
risks: Column widths must be fixed up front (longest label), or rows printed one at a time won't line up.
No view of the remaining steps, so the user can't see how far through the run is (no 'step 3 of 6' while running unless the status text says so).
The braille spinner from console.status needs a font that has braille (Cascadia does; legacy conhost fonts may not). Spinner 'line' (-\|/) is the safe fallback.
Moving warning logging out of _core into the CLI layer is a real refactor, not just a styling change.

patterns.name: Live checklist
patterns.summary: Every step appears up front as pending and is updated in place in a Rich Live table (glyph + label + detail), so the user sees the whole plan and where the run is. After a failure the remaining steps are marked 'skipped' rather than left frozen, and a single summary line follows when Live stops.

patterns.step_states: pending: '·' dim, label dim | running: 'dots' spinner cyan, label bold, elapsed seconds shown only after 0.5s | ok: '✓' green, label normal | warn: '!' bold yellow + 'WARN' word + hint sub-row | fail: 'x' bold red + 'FAILED' word + message/hint sub-rows | skipped: '-' dim + 'skipped'
patterns.header: One bold 'pkgdx init' line as the first row of the Live renderable (replaces both the rule and the reverse-video overall row).
patterns.success_summary: '6 ok in 2.9s' (or 'N ok, M warnings in Xs'), one line after Live stops.
patterns.warning_presentation: In the row: '!' glyph plus the word WARN and the detail, with a 'hint:' sub-row aligned to the detail column. Warnings are not logged above the display.
patterns.failure_presentation: The failed row gets 'x' and the word FAILED, with the cause, the parser message and a hint stacked in the detail column. Later steps turn to '-' skipped and the summary counts them. Expected errors show no traceback; with -d it prints after Live stops. Ctrl-C: the running row becomes '- <label>  interrupted', the remaining rows 'skipped', summary 'pkgdx init interrupted', exit 130.
patterns.state_change_reporting: The detail column shows Result.detail for every completed step, so created / updated / unchanged / reused is always visible.
patterns.non_tty_behaviour: Live is disabled. As each step finishes, its final row is printed (ASCII glyphs: '+', '!', 'x', '-'), then the summary. No pending rows or spinner. Example: ' + prek update --check         hook revisions up to date' / ' - detect-secrets scan         skipped' / 'pkgdx init failed: 2 ok, 1 failed, 3 skipped'.
risks: '✓' (U+2713) is in Cascadia Code/Mono (Windows Terminal default) but not in Consolas or other legacy console fonts. Keep an ASCII glyph map ('+') and use it for non-TTY output.
The full step list must be known up front. That's fine for init, but subcommands that work out their steps at runtime need to append rows.
Rich Live redraws can interleave badly with log records emitted mid-run; any logger output during Live must go through the same console (it does via RichHandler), but it will appear above the table.
Success output is 8 lines, longer than the minimal pattern. It still meets 'brief', but only just.

patterns.name: BLUF error card
patterns.summary: Built around the failure. While running, a single transient status line shows '[n/6] step'. On success it prints a two-line result. On an expected failure it prints a bordered error card whose title is the bottom line (what failed), with step, cause, fix, done/not-run and a debug hint. Unexpected errors keep the traceback, but only with -d.
patterns.mockup:
SUCCESS (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init: done in 2.9s
  changed: prek.toml (updated, 2 hooks added), .secrets.baseline (created)

(mid-run, transient)
⠼ pkgdx init  [5/6] prek update --check  1.1s

WARN (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init: done in 2.9s with 2 warnings
  ! identify Git top-level: not a Git repository, using project root
      -> Run `git init` to enable pre-commit hooks
  ! prek update --check: pkgdx v0.4.2 -> v0.5.0 available
      -> Update remote hook revisions - `prek update`
  changed: nothing

FAIL (TTY, final frame)
╭─ error: pkgdx init failed at 'configure pre-commit hooks' ───────────────────────╮
│ Cause    prek.toml could not be parsed                                           │
│          Invalid value (at line 12, column 9)                                    │
│ Fix      Fix prek.toml, or regenerate it with `pkgdx init --reset`               │
│ Done     identify project root, identify Git top-level                           │
│ Not run  prek install, prek update --check, detect-secrets scan                  │
╰───────────────────────────────────────── re-run with -d for the full traceback ─╯
patterns.step_states: n/a per step. Only one transient line: spinner + '[n/N]' + current label + elapsed (shown after 0.5s). Completed steps don't persist; outcome appears only in the result block.
patterns.header: None persistent. The transient status line carries 'pkgdx init [n/N] <step>'.
patterns.success_summary: 'pkgdx init: done in <elapsed>' plus one 'changed:' line listing the files created or updated (or 'changed: nothing').
patterns.warning_presentation: Collected during the run and printed after the summary line as a compact list: '!' + step label + detail, with a '->' hint on the next line. The heading carries the count ('with 2 warnings'), so it is never colour-only.
patterns.failure_presentation: Rich Panel (ROUNDED, red border, title bold) with BLUF title 'error: pkgdx init failed at <step>'. A two-column grid inside gives Cause (detail + message), Fix (hint), Done and Not run. The subtitle points to -d. No traceback for expected errors (a typed StepError / known exception map). Unexpected exceptions print a one-line 'unexpected error' card plus the Rich traceback and an issue-tracker link. Ctrl-C: 'pkgdx init: interrupted during prek update --check, no cleanup performed', exit 130.
patterns.state_change_reporting: Only changes are reported: a 'changed:' line aggregates details that are created/updated. Unchanged and reused items stay silent unless -v. This needs a small change-kind field on Result, or classification by keyword.
patterns.non_tty_behaviour: No panel, no spinner. GNU-style lines: success 'pkgdx init: done in 2.9s' + 'pkgdx init: changed prek.toml (updated, 2 hooks added)' per change. Warn 'pkgdx init: warning: identify Git top-level: not a Git repository, using project root' + '  hint: Run `git init` ...'. Fail 'pkgdx init: error: configure pre-commit hooks: prek.toml could not be parsed' + '  Invalid value (at line 12, column 9)' + '  hint: Fix prek.toml, or regenerate it with `pkgdx init --reset`' + '  not run: prek install, prek update --check, detect-secrets scan'.
risks: No record of completed steps on success. Users who want to see that the steps ran must use -v (a deliberate trade-off for brevity).
Panel box-drawing characters render in Windows Terminal. Rich falls back to ASCII on legacy_windows, but some fonts misalign wide rows, so narrow terminals wrap the card.

It needs a clear split between expected and unexpected errors (an exception-to-card mapping). If that split is wrong, real bugs get rewritten into friendly cards and their tracebacks are lost without -d.
The error-card helper can be reused by `pkgdx config` and other commands. That only pays off if those commands adopt it; otherwise it is a single-use abstraction (YAGNI).

patterns.name: Change receipt
patterns.summary: Philosophy: a run's output is a receipt of effects, not a step log. A transient spinner covers the run. The persistent output is grouped by effect (Changed / Needs attention / Unchanged) with a terraform-style count line. The non-TTY form is one logfmt record per step, which is greppable and stable.
patterns.mockup:
SUCCESS (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init  C:\src\acme
  Changed
    + prek.toml            updated, 2 hooks added
    + .secrets.baseline    created
  Unchanged  4  (root, Git top-level, Git shims, hook revisions)
Init complete: 2 changed, 4 unchanged, 0 warnings (2.9s)

WARN (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init  C:\src\acme
  Needs attention
    ! Git top-level        not a Git repository, using project root
                           -> Run `git init` to enable pre-commit hooks
    ! hook revisions       pkgdx v0.4.2 -> v0.5.0 available
                           -> Update remote hook revisions - `prek update`
  Changed
    + Git shims            installed at project root
  Unchanged  3  (root, prek.toml, .secrets.baseline)
Init complete: 1 changed, 3 unchanged, 2 warnings (2.9s)

FAIL (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init  C:\src\acme
  Failed
    x prek.toml            could not be parsed - Invalid value (at line 12, column 9)
                           -> Fix prek.toml, or regenerate it with `pkgdx init --reset`
  Not applied  3  (prek install, prek update --check, detect-secrets scan)
Init failed: 0 changed, 2 unchanged, 1 failed, 3 not applied
patterns.step_states: n/a in final frame (grouped by effect). During run: one transient 'dots' spinner line with the current step label. In the receipt: '+' changed, '=' / count unchanged, '!' warn (bold yellow), 'x' fail (bold red), with section headings in words.
patterns.header: 'pkgdx init  <project root>' once, printed when the receipt is rendered (the root is the run's context).
patterns.success_summary: Terraform-style count line: 'Init complete: N changed, N unchanged, N warnings (elapsed)'.
patterns.warning_presentation: A 'Needs attention' section listed first, with '!' + object + detail and a '->' hint aligned beneath. The count line repeats the warning total.
patterns.failure_presentation: A 'Failed' section at the top with cause, parser message and '->' fix, then 'Not applied' with a count and names, then an 'Init failed:' count line. No traceback unless -d. Ctrl-C: 'Interrupted' section naming the in-flight step plus 'Not applied' list, 'Init interrupted: no cleanup performed', exit 130.
patterns.state_change_reporting: This is the centre of the pattern. Each Result is classified as changed, unchanged or attention and grouped. The proper fix is an explicit `change: created|updated|unchanged` field on Result; the demo can classify by keywords (created/updated/added/installed vs unchanged/reused/already/up to date).
patterns.non_tty_behaviour: logfmt, one record per step as it completes, then a summary record. E.g. 'init step="configure pre-commit hooks" status=ok change=updated detail="prek.toml updated, 2 hooks added"' ... 'init status=fail changed=0 unchanged=2 failed=1 not_applied=3'. Warnings and failures add hint="...".
risks: Classifying changes by keywords in the detail string is fragile. A real implementation needs _core functions to return a change kind, which touches _core's API.
Grouping by effect hides the order the steps ran in, so it is harder to tell which step produced which effect when debugging.

The logfmt non-TTY output looks machine-readable and could become a de-facto interface. §4/§10 say machine output belongs behind --json and must not change without notice, so it should be clearly documented as human/CI text, or be the --json shape.
Naming objects ('Git shims', 'hook revisions') instead of steps needs a per-step object name, which is another field to maintain.

patterns.name: Collapsing phase tree
patterns.summary: A live Rich Tree groups the six steps into three phases (Locate, Configure, Verify). A phase that ends all-ok collapses to a single line with its count and the key change. A phase with a warning or failure stays expanded, with hints as child nodes. The hierarchy carries over to other subcommands (e.g. `pkgdx config` sources as phases).
patterns.mockup:
SUCCESS (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init  C:\src\acme
├── ✓ Locate      2/2  project root + Git top-level C:\src\acme
├── ✓ Configure   2/2  prek.toml updated (2 hooks added); Git shims already installed
└── ✓ Verify      2/2  hook revisions up to date; .secrets.baseline created
done in 2.9s

(mid-run frame)
pkgdx init  C:\src\acme
├── ✓ Locate      2/2  project root + Git top-level C:\src\acme
├── ✓ Configure   2/2  prek.toml updated (2 hooks added); Git shims already installed
└── ⠼ Verify      0/2
    ├── ⠼ prek update --check   1.1s
    └── · detect-secrets scan

WARN (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init  C:\src\acme
├── ! Locate      2/2  1 warning
│   ├── ✓ identify project root    C:\src\acme (pyproject.toml)
│   └── ! identify Git top-level   WARN not a Git repository, using project root
│       └── hint: Run `git init` to enable pre-commit hooks
├── ✓ Configure   2/2  prek.toml unchanged; Git shims installed at project root
└── ! Verify      2/2  1 warning
    ├── ! prek update --check      WARN pkgdx v0.4.2 -> v0.5.0 available
    │   └── hint: Update remote hook revisions - `prek update`
    └── ✓ detect-secrets scan      .secrets.baseline exists, reused
done in 2.9s with 2 warnings

FAIL (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init  C:\src\acme
├── ✓ Locate      2/2  project root + Git top-level C:\src\acme
├── x Configure   FAILED at 1/2
│   ├── x configure pre-commit hooks   FAILED prek.toml could not be parsed
│   │   ├── Invalid value (at line 12, column 9)
│   │   └── hint: Fix prek.toml, or regenerate it with `pkgdx init --reset`
│   └── - prek install                 skipped
└── - Verify      skipped
pkgdx init failed in Configure (1 failed, 3 skipped)
patterns.step_states: pending: '·' dim | running: 'dots' spinner cyan + elapsed after 0.5s | ok: '✓' green (phase collapses when all ok) | warn: '!' bold yellow + 'WARN' word, phase stays expanded | fail: 'x' bold red + 'FAILED' word, phase expanded, later phases '- skipped' dim
patterns.header: Tree root label 'pkgdx init  <project root>' (the only title).
patterns.warning_presentation: The phase gets '!' and 'N warning(s)' and stays expanded. The step node shows WARN + detail, and a 'hint:' child node gives the next action.
patterns.failure_presentation: The failing phase and step are marked 'x' FAILED and stay expanded, with the parser message and hint as child nodes. The phase's remaining steps and all later phases are marked '- skipped'. The summary names the phase and gives counts. Traceback only with -d. Ctrl-C: in-flight node becomes '- interrupted', summary 'pkgdx init interrupted in Verify, no cleanup performed', exit 130.
patterns.state_change_reporting: Collapsed phase lines join the step details with ';' (so 'prek.toml updated (2 hooks added)' stays visible). Expanded phases show the details per step.
patterns.non_tty_behaviour: Live is disabled. When each phase finishes, its final subtree is printed using ASCII guides (Tree guide chars swapped for '|--' / '`--'), then the summary. No pending nodes or spinners. Example: 'pkgdx init  C:\src\acme' / '|-- + Locate      2/2  project root + Git top-level C:\src\acme' / '`-- - Verify      skipped' / 'pkgdx init failed in Configure (1 failed, 3 skipped)'.
risks: The phase grouping is new information the scenarios don't carry. It has to be defined per command, which is extra structure that may break YAGNI for a 6-step run.
Collapsed lines that join details with ';' can exceed 100 columns and wrap, which spoils the tree's alignment.
Rich Tree guides use box-drawing characters ('├──'). They render in Windows Terminal, but non-TTY needs an explicit ASCII guide style. The '✓' glyph needs Cascadia (ASCII '+' fallback).
Most moving parts of the set: Live + Tree rebuilds + collapse logic. Collapsing nodes can make the display height jump during the run.

patterns.name: Verb ledger (uv / cargo)
patterns.summary: Borrows from uv and cargo: each step becomes one terse past-tense line with a right-aligned bold verb (Resolved, Updated, Created, Reused), printed only when the step finishes. A transient spinner status line shows only the in-flight step, and the title is the first and only header.

(live: while 'prek update --check' runs, a spinner line '  ⠋ Checking hook revisions' sits at the bottom and is erased on completion)
patterns.step_states: pending: not shown (no list of future steps). running: single transient bottom line with Rich status spinner (dots, ASCII fallback '|/-\\') plus the step label, dim. ok: permanent line with bold green right-aligned verb in a 10-col field; unchanged uses dim verb 'Unchanged'. warn: bold yellow 'warning' verb. fail: bold red 'error' verb, then bold red 'Failed' summary verb. Verb word carries the state, so NO_COLOR still reads correctly.
patterns.header: One line: bold 'pkgdx init' plus dim project root. No rule, no second title row.
patterns.success_summary: 'Finished  6 steps in 2.9s' with bold green verb; omit the step count when all unchanged and print 'Finished  nothing to change' instead.
patterns.warning_presentation: Inline in sequence as a yellow 'warning' verb line carrying Result.detail; hints collected after the summary as git-style 'hint' lines (dim verb, normal text) so next actions land last, where the eye ends. Summary counts warnings.
patterns.failure_presentation: Red 'error' line with detail and message, one 'hint' line, then red 'Failed' summary stating progress (2 of 6). No traceback for expected errors; a dim pointer to -d. Overall status is final, never a frozen spinner.
patterns.state_change_reporting: Carried by the verb itself: Created / Updated / Reused / Unchanged / Installed, derived from Result.detail. Every state change is visible without -d.
patterns.non_tty_behaviour: Identical lines without colour, without the spinner and without right-alignment padding changes (same 10-col field so it greps well). Lines flush as steps finish. Header line is kept. Example plain line: '    Updated  prek.toml, 2 hooks added'.
guidance_refs: standard-cli §4 brief output on success and inform on state change
toolchain-logging §3 stderr via console, TTY check on the written stream
risks: Verb vocabulary must be derived from Result.detail (or extend Result with a verb field), mild coupling
Hints appearing after the summary requires collecting them in a list
Right-aligned verbs need a fixed 10-col width; long verbs would overflow
Ctrl-C (obs 8) not handled by layout alone; needs a KeyboardInterrupt wrapper printing 'Interrupted' and exiting 130

patterns.name: Boot-log text badges (systemd)
patterns.summary: Borrows from systemd boot output: every line starts with a fixed-width 6-char text badge [ OK ] / [WARN] / [FAIL] / [ .. ] followed by the step label and detail. The running line is redrawn in place and then committed with its final badge, so state is legible without colour or Unicode glyphs.

[ OK ] configure pre-commit hooks .... prek.toml updated, 2 hooks added
[ OK ] prek install .................. Git shims already installed
[ OK ] prek update --check ........... hook revisions up to date
[ OK ] detect-secrets scan ........... .secrets.baseline created

WARN
[ OK ] identify project root ........ C:\src\acme (pyproject.toml)
[WARN] identify Git top-level ........ not a Git repository, using project root
[ OK ] configure pre-commit hooks .... prek.toml unchanged
[ OK ] prek install .................. Git shims installed at project root
[WARN] prek update --check ........... pkgdx v0.4.2 -> v0.5.0 available
[ OK ] detect-secrets scan ........... .secrets.baseline exists, reused
       2 warnings: git init | prek update

FAIL

[ OK ] identify Git top-level ........ C:\src\acme
[FAIL] configure pre-commit hooks .... prek.toml could not be parsed
       Invalid value (at line 12, column 9)
       hint: Fix prek.toml, or regenerate it with `pkgdx init --reset`
[SKIP] prek install
[SKIP] prek update --check

patterns.step_states: pending: not shown (or optionally dim '[    ]' if listing ahead). running: '[ .. ]' with a spinner-cycling cell (|/-\\) redrawn in place via Live. ok: '[ OK ]' bold green. warn: '[WARN]' bold yellow. fail: '[FAIL]' bold red. skipped (after a failure): dim '[SKIP]' so remaining steps are not mistaken for pending. Badge text, not colour, is the signal.
patterns.header: None. The badges are self-explanatory and the command name is already on the user's prompt line. Optionally one dim 'pkgdx init' line.
patterns.success_summary: No separate summary: the all-OK column is the summary. Optional dim last line '6 ok in 2.9s' only when interactive.
patterns.warning_presentation: Badge [WARN] on the step line with the detail text; one dim indented line at the end lists warning hints compactly. Hints on warnings are kept to a single line each, indented under the badge column (7 spaces).
patterns.failure_presentation: [FAIL] row, then indented message and 'hint:' lines directly beneath, remaining steps [SKIP]. No traceback; -d adds it. Exit code 1.
patterns.state_change_reporting: Detail column carries created/updated/unchanged/reused wording verbatim from Result.detail; no extra work needed.
patterns.non_tty_behaviour: Same text with no Live: each line printed once, on completion, with its final badge, no ANSI. Dot leaders keep columns aligned so it is grep-friendly ('grep ^\[FAIL\]').
guidance_refs: standard-cli §5 consider where the user looks first
risks: Dot leaders and detail column truncate/wrap on narrow terminals (<80 cols); must compute width from console.width
Looks dated or noisy to some users; no emphasis on what actually changed
Showing [SKIP] rows needs the pattern to iterate the remaining steps after a FAIL
Ctrl-C handling still to be added (print '[ !! ] interrupted', exit 130)

patterns.name: Arrow sections with indented detail (Homebrew)
patterns.summary: Borrows from Homebrew: each step is a bold '==> label' arrow heading and its result is an indented detail line beneath, with git-style 'hint:' lines for next actions. A narrative top-to-bottom transcript, not a dashboard.
patterns.mockup:
SUCCESS
==> Identifying project root

patterns.step_states: pending: not shown. running: the arrow heading is printed immediately in bold blue and a transient spinner sits on the line below it, replaced by the detail line. ok: detail line plain (heading turns bold green only in colour; no glyph needed). warn: detail line prefixed literal 'Warning:' in bold yellow. fail: prefixed literal 'Error:' in bold red. patterns.failure_presentation: Inline 'Error:' prefix, message on following indented line, 'hint:' line, then '==> Failed after 2 steps' in bold red. Output ends on the failure so BLUF holds for the reader at the bottom.
patterns.state_change_reporting: The indented detail line is the state report ('prek.toml updated', '.secrets.baseline created'); optionally make the changed noun bold.
patterns.non_tty_behaviour: Identical text with colour stripped; headings are only printed when the step starts, so a hung step is visible in a CI log. No spinner. Headings and details are one write each.

risks: Roughly doubles the line count (12+ lines vs 6) which conflicts with 'keep it brief' in §4
Needs progressive-form labels ('Identifying...') instead of the existing imperative labels in _cli.py
Heading printed before the result means a warning appears after its heading, spreads one step across two lines
Ctrl-C needs a wrapper (print '==> Interrupted', exit 130)

patterns.header: Bold 'pkgdx init' single line, no rule.
patterns.success_summary: None beyond the all-check list; optionally dim 'done in 2.9s' footer.
patterns.warning_presentation: Warning state is in the row (bang glyph plus 'warning:' text) and the hints are gathered under a '2 warnings' footer block, because hints are usually actions and benefit from being grouped.

Live redraw flicker if the table is taller than the terminal
Needs a row-state holder (one small class or dict) to render pending/running/done
Showing all pending rows up front means a failed run leaves rows that never ran; skipped marking requires handling
Ctrl-C needs Live stop plus 'interrupted' row, exit 130

patterns.summary: Borrows from git and cargo: show a single transient status line while working, then print only what changed or needs attention, followed by one terse summary. Unchanged and routine steps are collapsed into the summary count, matching the common idempotent re-run of init.

patterns.step_states: pending: not shown. running: one transient spinner line with step index and label (the single place M/N survives, because it is useful only while waiting). ok: no row unless the step changed state. warn: 'warning:' prefix in bold yellow. fail: 'error:' prefix in bold red. changed: dim-free bold verb (created/updated). Text prefixes carry state.
patterns.success_summary: One line: 'init finished in 2.9s: N changed, M unchanged' (or 'nothing to change'), summary verb bold green.
patterns.warning_presentation: Warnings are printed as they occur, 'warning:' prefix plus 'hint:' line beneath, and counted in the summary. This is the closest to today's log-line behaviour but with consistent wording.
patterns.failure_presentation: BLUF: 'error:' line, detail, 'hint:' line, and a one-line summary naming the failed step and index. No traceback for expected failures; unexpected exceptions still go through the logger with traceback.
patterns.state_change_reporting: This pattern's focus: only created/updated steps get a line, derived from Result.detail; 'unchanged'/'reused' counted in the summary. Satisfies 'when changing state, inform the user' with minimal noise.
patterns.non_tty_behaviour: Same lines minus the spinner. Because success is already short, piped output is naturally brief: just the changed lines and the summary. With --plain the prefixes stay.
guidance_refs: standard-cli §4 keep it brief, inform on state change
risks: Users cannot see that each step ran, so trust relies on the summary; hide-by-default may feel too sparse for first-time users (mitigate with -v listing all steps)
Requires classifying a step as changed or unchanged, which means parsing Result.detail or adding a flag to the result
Classifying 'unchanged' wrongly would hide real changes
Ctrl-C needs a wrapper (print 'init interrupted', exit 130)

patterns.state_change_reporting: Detail column on the tally rows (created/updated/unchanged), dim for unchanged, normal for changed.

rustc idiom may feel heavy for a setup command
Collected blocks mean a warning is only visible after the run ends, which delays awareness on long steps unless streamed
Ctrl-C needs a wrapper printing 'pkgdx init: interrupted'
